   157→
   158→def _missing_scored_dimensions(
   159→    *,
   160→    selected_dims: list[str],
   161→    scored_dims: list[str],
   162→) -> list[str]:
   163→    selected = set(selected_dims)
   164→    return [dim for dim in scored_dims if dim not in selected]
   165→
   166→
   167→def _missing_dimensions_command(*, missing_dims: list[str], scan_path: str) -> str:
   168→    """Return rerun command for missing subjective dimensions."""
   169→    base = "desloppify review --run-batches --runner codex --parallel --scan-after-import"
   170→    if scan_path and scan_path != ".":
   171→        base += f" --path {shlex.quote(scan_path)}"
   172→    if missing_dims:
   173→        base += f" --dimensions {','.join(missing_dims)}"
   174→    return base
   175→
   176→
   177→def _print_preflight_dimension_scope_notice(
   178→    *,
   179→    selected_dims: list[str],
   180→    scored_dims: list[str],
   181→    explicit_selection: bool,
   182→    scan_path: str,
   183→    colorize_fn,
   184→) -> None:
   185→    """Print trigger-time notice when run scope is a scored-dimension subset."""
   186→    if not scored_dims:
   187→        return
   188→    missing_dims = _missing_scored_dimensions(
   189→        selected_dims=selected_dims,
   190→        scored_dims=scored_dims,
   191→    )
   192→    if not missing_dims:
   193→        return
   194→
   195→    covered_count = len([dim for dim in selected_dims if dim in set(scored_dims)])
   196→    scope_reason = (
   197→        "explicit --dimensions selection"
   198→        if explicit_selection
   199→        else "language default review dimension set"
   200→    )
   201→    tone = "yellow" if explicit_selection else "red"
   202→    print(
   203→        colorize_fn(
   204→            "  WARNING: this run targets "
   205→            f"{covered_count}/{len(scored_dims)} scored subjective dimensions "
   206→            f"({scope_reason}).",
   207→            tone,
   208→        )
   209→    )
   210→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   211→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   212→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   213→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Missing from this run: {preview}", "yellow"))
   214→    print(
   215→        colorize_fn(
   216→            "  Rerun missing dimensions: "
   217→            f"`{_missing_dimensions_command(missing_dims=missing_dims, scan_path=scan_path)}`",
   218→            "dim",
   219→        )
   220→    )
   221→
   222→
   223→def _print_import_dimension_coverage_notice(
   224→    *,
   225→    assessed_dims: list[str],
   226→    scored_dims: list[str],
   227→    scan_path: str,
   228→    colorize_fn,
   229→) -> list[str]:
   230→    """Print result-time notice when merged import covers only a subset."""
   231→    if not scored_dims:
   232→        return []
   233→    missing_dims = _missing_scored_dimensions(
   234→        selected_dims=assessed_dims,
   235→        scored_dims=scored_dims,
   236→    )
   237→    if not missing_dims:
   238→        return []
   239→
   240→    covered_count = len([dim for dim in assessed_dims if dim in set(scored_dims)])
   241→    print(
   242→        colorize_fn(
   243→            "  Coverage gap: imported assessments for "
   244→            f"{covered_count}/{len(scored_dims)} scored subjective dimensions.",
   245→            "yellow",
   246→        )
   247→    )
   248→    preview = ", ".join(missing_dims[:5])
   249→    if len(missing_dims) > 5:
   250→        preview = f"{preview}, +{len(missing_dims) - 5} more"
   251→    print(colorize_fn(f"  Still missing: {preview}", "yellow"))
   252→    print(
   253→        colorize_fn(
   254→            "  Run to cover missing dimensions: "
   255→            f"`{_missing_dimensions_command(missing_dims=missing_dims, scan_path=scan_path)}`",
   256→            "dim",
   257→        )
   258→    )
   259→    return missing_dims

   262→def _append_run_log_line(run_log_path: Path, message: str) -> None:
   263→    """Append one timestamped line to the run log (best effort)."""
   264→    line = f"{datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec='seconds')} {message}\n"
   265→    try:
   266→        with run_log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   267→            handle.write(line)
   268→    except OSError:
   269→        return

   273→    *,
   274→    prompt: str,
   275→    output_file: Path,
   276→    log_file: Path,
   277→    project_root: Path,
   278→    run_codex_batch_fn,

   289→def _run_batch_task(
   290→    *,
   291→    batch_index: int,
   292→    prompt_path: Path,
   293→    output_path: Path,
   294→    log_path: Path,
   295→    project_root: Path,
   296→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   297→) -> int:
   298→    """Read one prompt artifact and execute its runner task."""
   299→    try:
   300→        prompt = prompt_path.read_text()
   301→    except OSError as exc:
   302→        raise RuntimeError(
   303→            f"unable to read prompt for batch #{batch_index + 1}: {prompt_path}"
   304→        ) from exc
   305→    return _run_batch_prompt(
   306→        prompt=prompt,
   307→        output_file=output_path,
   308→        log_file=log_path,
   309→        project_root=project_root,
   310→        run_codex_batch_fn=run_codex_batch_fn,

   314→def _build_batch_tasks(
   315→    *,
   316→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   317→    prompt_files: dict[int, Path],
   318→    output_files: dict[int, Path],
   319→    log_files: dict[int, Path],
   320→    project_root: Path,
   321→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   322→) -> dict[int, object]:
   323→    """Build index→callable task map for execute_batches."""
   324→    tasks: dict[int, object] = {}
   325→    for batch_index in selected_indexes:
   326→        tasks[batch_index] = partial(
   327→            _run_batch_task,
   328→            batch_index=batch_index,
   329→            prompt_path=prompt_files[batch_index],
   330→            output_path=output_files[batch_index],
   331→            log_path=log_files[batch_index],
   332→            project_root=project_root,
   333→            run_codex_batch_fn=run_codex_batch_fn,
   334→        )
   335→    return tasks

   390→        "batch_heartbeat_seconds": heartbeat_seconds if run_parallel else None,
   391→        "batch_stall_warning_seconds": stall_warning_seconds if run_parallel else None,
   392→        "batch_stall_kill_seconds": stall_kill_seconds,

   404→    safe_write_text_fn(run_summary_path, json.dumps(run_summary, indent=2) + "\n")

   409→def do_run_batches(
   410→    args,
   411→    state,
   412→    lang,
   413→    state_file,
   414→    *,
   415→    config: dict | None,
   416→    run_stamp_fn,
   417→    load_or_prepare_packet_fn,
   418→    selected_batch_indexes_fn,
   419→    prepare_run_artifacts_fn,
   420→    run_codex_batch_fn,
   421→    execute_batches_fn,
   422→    collect_batch_results_fn,
   423→    print_failures_fn,
   424→    print_failures_and_exit_fn,
   425→    merge_batch_results_fn,
   426→    build_import_provenance_fn,
   427→    do_import_fn,
   428→    run_followup_scan_fn,
   429→    safe_write_text_fn,
   430→    colorize_fn,
   431→    project_root: Path,
   432→    subagent_runs_dir: Path,
   433→) -> None:
   434→    """Run holistic investigation batches with a local subagent runner."""
   435→    config = config or {}
   436→    runner = getattr(args, "runner", "codex")
   437→    _validate_runner(runner, colorize_fn=colorize_fn)
   438→    allow_partial = bool(getattr(args, "allow_partial", False))
   439→    policy = resolve_batch_run_policy(args)
   440→    run_parallel = policy.run_parallel
   441→    max_parallel_batches = policy.max_parallel_batches
   442→    heartbeat_seconds = policy.heartbeat_seconds
   443→    batch_timeout_seconds = policy.batch_timeout_seconds
   444→    batch_max_retries = policy.batch_max_retries
   445→    batch_retry_backoff_seconds = policy.batch_retry_backoff_seconds
   446→    stall_warning_seconds = policy.stall_warning_seconds
   447→    stall_kill_seconds = policy.stall_kill_seconds
   448→
   449→    stamp = run_stamp_fn()
   450→    packet, immutable_packet_path, prompt_packet_path = load_or_prepare_packet_fn(
   451→        args,
   452→        state=state,
   453→        lang=lang,
   454→        config=config,
   455→        stamp=stamp,
   456→    )
   457→
   458→    scan_path = str(getattr(args, "path", ".") or ".")
   459→    packet_dimensions = _normalize_dimension_list(packet.get("dimensions", []))
   460→    scored_dimensions = _scored_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   461→    _print_preflight_dimension_scope_notice(
   462→        selected_dims=packet_dimensions,
   463→        scored_dims=scored_dimensions,
   464→        explicit_selection=bool(getattr(args, "dimensions", None)),
   465→        scan_path=scan_path,
   466→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   467→    )
   468→    suggested_prepare_cmd = f"desloppify review --prepare --path {scan_path}"
   469→    batches = _require_batches(
   470→        packet,
   471→        colorize_fn=colorize_fn,
   472→        suggested_prepare_cmd=suggested_prepare_cmd,
   473→    )
   474→
   475→    selected_indexes = selected_batch_indexes_fn(args, batch_count=len(batches))
   476→    total_batches = len(selected_indexes)
   477→    effective_workers = min(total_batches, max_parallel_batches) if run_parallel else 1
   478→    waves = max(1, math.ceil(total_batches / max(1, effective_workers)))
   479→    worst_case_seconds = waves * batch_timeout_seconds
   480→    worst_case_minutes = max(1, math.ceil(worst_case_seconds / 60))
   481→    print(
   482→        colorize_fn(
   483→            "  Runtime expectation: "
   484→            f"{total_batches} batch(es), workers={effective_workers}, "
   485→            f"timeout-per-batch={int(batch_timeout_seconds / 60)}m, "
   486→            f"worst-case upper bound ~{worst_case_minutes}m.",
   487→            "dim",
   488→        )
   489→    )
   490→    run_dir, logs_dir, prompt_files, output_files, log_files = prepare_run_artifacts_fn(
   491→        stamp=stamp,
   492→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   493→        batches=batches,
   494→        packet_path=prompt_packet_path,
   495→        run_root=subagent_runs_dir,
   496→        repo_root=project_root,
   497→    )
   498→    raw_run_log_file = getattr(args, "run_log_file", None)
   499→    run_log_file_value = (
   500→        raw_run_log_file.strip()

## Summary: `batch_stall_kill_seconds` Implementation

I've thoroughly analyzed the desloppify codebase to understand how stall detection works. Here's the complete picture:

### 1. **STALL DETECTION - What Counts as "Output"**

Location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_process.py`, lines 232-264 in `_check_stall()` function

The stall detection mechanism tracks **two independent signals**:

**A. Output File Signature (primary signal)**
- Computes a tuple of `(file_size_bytes, modification_timestamp)` from the output file
- If the signature **hasn't changed** for `threshold` seconds (stall_kill_seconds), AND
- The stream activity **hasn't changed** for `threshold` seconds,
- Then the process is considered stalled

**B. Stream Activity (secondary signal)**
- Every line read from stdout/stderr updates `last_stream_activity` timestamp (line 177 in `_drain_stream()`)
- Both output file stability AND stream idle time must exceed threshold to trigger stall

**Key Implementation Details** (lines 243-267):
```python
def _check_stall(output_file, prev_sig, prev_stable, now, last_activity, threshold):
    """Returns (stalled, new_sig, new_stable_since)"""
    # Get current file signature (size + mtime)
    current_signature = (stat.st_size, stat.st_mtime)
    
    # Case 1: No output file yet - check silent hang
    if current_signature is None:
        output_age = now - prev_stable
        stream_idle = now - last_activity
        # Stalled if BOTH output age AND stream idle exceed threshold
        if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
            return True, None, baseline
    
    # Case 2: Output changed - reset stall timer
    if current_signature != prev_sig:
        return False, current_signature, now  # Reset to now
    
    # Case 3: Output stable - check if stable long enough
    output_age = now - prev_stable
    stream_idle = now - last_activity
    if output_age >= threshold and stream_idle >= threshold:
        return True, prev_sig, prev_stable
```

**What Resets the Timer:**
- Any change to output file (size OR modification time)
- Any output from stdout/stderr streams

---

### 2. **PROCESS TERMINATION - Exit Code 124**

Location: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/runner_process.py`, lines 496-531 in `_handle_timeout_or_stall()` function

When stall is detected:

1. **Process is killed** (lines 349-350):
   ```python
   recovered_from_stall = _output_file_has_json_payload(ctx.output_file)
   _terminate_process(process)
   ```

2. **Termination sequence** (lines 146-164 in `_terminate_process()`):
   - First tries `process.terminate()` with 3-second wait
   - If that fails, tries `process.kill()` with 3-second wait
   - If both fail, gives up gracefully

3. **Exit code determination** (lines 519-531):
   - **If output file contains valid JSON payload** → returns **0** (success recovery)
   - **If NO valid JSON payload** → returns **124** (standard Unix timeout code)
   - Log entry: `"Recovered stalled batch from JSON output file; continuing as success."`

Exit code 124 is the standard Unix signal for timeout (SIGTERM = 15 + 109 = 124 in some shells, but it's a convention for timeout scenarios).

---

### 3. **CONFIGURATION - Where `batch_stall_kill_seconds` is Set**

**A. Default Value** (line 21 in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/runtime/policy.py`):
```python
DEFAULT_BATCH_STALL_KILL_SECONDS = 120
```

**B. Policy Resolution** (lines 49-85 in `policy.py`):
```python
def resolve_batch_run_policy(args) -> BatchRunPolicy:
    stall_kill_seconds=_coerce_non_negative_int(
        getattr(args, "batch_stall_kill_seconds", None),
        default=DEFAULT_BATCH_STALL_KILL_SECONDS,
    )
```

**C. Configuration Flow:**
1. CLI arg: `--batch-stall-kill-seconds` (passed to args)
2. Policy object: `BatchRunPolicy.stall_kill_seconds` (line 35)
3. Passed to runner: `CodexBatchRunnerDeps.stall_after_output_seconds` (line 256 in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/batch.py`)

**D. Usage in Batch Execution** (lines 243-259 in `batch.py`):

**E. Execution via Popen** (lines 267-368 in `runner_process.py`):

- Checks stall every iteration (line 334)
- If stalled, terminates immediately (line 350)

| **Stall Condition** | Output stable ≥ threshold AND stream idle ≥ threshold |
| **Process Kill Signal** | `terminate()` then `kill()` (graceful → hard) |
| **Exit Code on Stall** | 124 (if no JSON output) or 0 (if JSON recovered) |
| **Configuration** | CLI arg `--batch-stall-kill-seconds`, env via policy.py |
| **Execution Model** | Popen with live streaming threads + main loop stall checks |

1→"""Preflight guards for subjective review reruns.
     2→
     3→Blocks reruns while backlog remains (objective findings and/or subjective queue
     4→work), unless ``--force-review-rerun`` is set. Also clears stale subjective
     5→markers before a new cycle.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→import re
    11→import sys
    12→
    13→from desloppify.core.output_api import colorize
    14→from desloppify.engine.plan import compute_subjective_visibility

    16→from desloppify.state import StateModel, save_state

    18→from .helpers import parse_dimensions

    20→
    21→def clear_stale_subjective_entries(
    22→    state: StateModel,
    23→    *,
    24→    dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
    25→) -> list[str]:
    26→    """Clear ``needs_review_refresh`` markers from subjective assessments.
    27→
    28→    When *dimensions* is provided, only those dimensions are cleared;
    29→    otherwise all stale dimensions are cleared.
    30→
    31→    Returns the list of dimension keys that were cleared.
    32→    """
    33→    assessments: dict = state.get("subjective_assessments", {})
    34→    cleared: list[str] = []
    35→    for dim_key, assessment in assessments.items():
    36→        if not isinstance(assessment, dict):
    37→            continue
    38→        if dimensions is not None and dim_key not in dimensions:
    39→            continue
    40→        if assessment.get("needs_review_refresh"):
    41→            assessment.pop("needs_review_refresh", None)
    42→            assessment.pop("stale_since", None)
    43→            assessment.pop("refresh_reason", None)
    44→            cleared.append(dim_key)
    45→    return cleared
    46→
    47→
    48→def _scored_dimensions(state: StateModel) -> list[str]:
    49→    """Return dimension keys that already have a nonzero subjective score."""
    50→    assessments: dict = state.get("subjective_assessments", {})
    51→    scored: list[str] = []
    52→    for dim_key, assessment in assessments.items():
    53→        if isinstance(assessment, dict):
    54→            if assessment.get("score", 0):
    55→                scored.append(dim_key)
    56→        elif isinstance(assessment, (int, float)) and assessment:
    57→            scored.append(dim_key)
    58→    return sorted(scored)
    59→
    60→
    61→def _normalize_dimension_key(raw: object) -> str:
    62→    """Normalize a dimension key/name to canonical snake_case."""
    63→    text = str(raw or "").strip().lower().replace(" ", "_")
    64→    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]+", "_", text).strip("_")
    65→
    66→
    67→def _count_open_subjective_queue_items(
    68→    state: StateModel,
    69→    *,
    70→    dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
    71→    policy=None,
    72→) -> int:
    73→    """Count open synthetic subjective queue items for rerun gating."""
    74→    normalized_dims = (
    75→        {_normalize_dimension_key(dim) for dim in dimensions}
    76→        if dimensions is not None
    77→        else None
    78→    )
    79→    queue = build_work_queue(
    80→        state,
    81→        options=QueueBuildOptions(
    82→            status="open",
    83→            include_subjective=True,
    84→            count=None,
    85→            policy=policy,
    86→        ),
    87→    )
    88→    count = 0
    89→    for item in queue.get("items", []):
    90→        if item.get("kind") != "subjective_dimension":
    91→            continue
    92→        # Stale reruns are not blocking backlog — they ARE the work
    93→        if item.get("stale_review"):
    94→            continue
    95→        if normalized_dims is None:
    96→            count += 1
    97→            continue
    98→        detail = item.get("detail")
    99→        raw_dim = detail.get("dimension", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   100→        item_dim = _normalize_dimension_key(raw_dim)
   101→        if item_dim and item_dim in normalized_dims:
   102→            count += 1
   103→    return count
   104→
   105→
   106→def _blocking_scored_dimensions(
   107→    state: StateModel,
   108→    *,
   109→    dimensions: set[str] | None,
   110→    normalized_dimensions: set[str] | None,
   111→) -> list[str]:
   112→    scored_dims = _scored_dimensions(state)
   113→    if dimensions is None:
   114→        return scored_dims
   115→    normalized = normalized_dimensions or set()
   116→    return sorted(
   117→        dim
   118→        for dim in scored_dims
   119→        if _normalize_dimension_key(dim) in normalized
   120→    )
   121→
   122→
   123→def _objective_and_subjective_backlog(
   124→    state: StateModel,
   125→    *,
   126→    blocking_dims: list[str],
   127→) -> tuple[int, int]:
   128→    policy = compute_subjective_visibility(state)
   129→    objective_total = policy.objective_count
   130→    subjective_total = _count_open_subjective_queue_items(
   131→        state,
   132→        dimensions=set(blocking_dims),
   133→        policy=policy,
   134→    )
   135→    return objective_total, subjective_total
   136→
   137→
   138→def _print_backlog_blocked_message(
   139→    *,
   140→    blocking_dims: list[str],
   141→    objective_total: int,
   142→    subjective_total: int,
   143→    dimensions: set[str] | None,
   144→) -> None:
   145→    print(
   146→        colorize(
   147→            "  Blocked: rerun requires drained backlog "
   148→            f"(objective: {objective_total}, subjective: {subjective_total}).",
   149→            "red",
   150→        ),
   151→        file=sys.stderr,
   152→    )
   153→    print(
   154→        colorize(
   155→            f"  Scored dimensions: {', '.join(blocking_dims)}",
   156→            "yellow",
   157→        ),
   158→        file=sys.stderr,
   159→    )
   160→    if objective_total > 0:
   161→        print(
   162→            colorize(
   163→                f"  Open objective finding(s): {objective_total}",
   164→                "yellow",
   165→            ),
   166→            file=sys.stderr,
   167→        )
   168→    if subjective_total > 0:
   169→        print(
   170→            colorize(
   171→                f"  Open subjective queue item(s): {subjective_total}",
   172→                "yellow",
   173→            ),
   174→            file=sys.stderr,
   175→        )
   176→    print("", file=sys.stderr)
   177→    if dimensions is not None:
   178→        unscored = sorted(dimensions - set(blocking_dims))
   179→        if unscored:
   180→            print(
   181→                colorize(
   182→                    f"  Tip: target only unscored dimensions with "
   183→                    f"--dimensions {','.join(unscored)}",
   184→                    "dim",
   185→                ),
   186→                file=sys.stderr,
   187→            )
   188→    print(
   189→        colorize(
   190→            "  Resolve open items first, or override with --force-review-rerun",
   191→            "dim",
   192→        ),
   193→        file=sys.stderr,
   194→    )
   195→
   196→
   197→def review_rerun_preflight(
   198→    state: StateModel,
   199→    args,
   200→    *,
   201→    state_file=None,
   202→    save_fn=save_state,
   203→) -> None:
   204→    """Single entry point: gate check -> clear stale -> save.
   205→
   206→    Exits with code 1 when open backlog exists and ``--force-review-rerun`` is
   207→    not set. On success, clears stale subjective markers for targeted
   208→    dimensions and persists state.
   209→    """
   210→    dimensions = parse_dimensions(args)
   211→    normalized_dimensions = (
   212→        {_normalize_dimension_key(dim) for dim in dimensions}
   213→        if dimensions is not None
   214→        else None
   215→    )
   216→
   217→    # --force-review-rerun bypasses the gate
   218→    if getattr(args, "force_review_rerun", False):
   219→        print(
   220→            colorize(
   221→                "  --force-review-rerun: bypassing rerun backlog checks.",
   222→                "yellow",
   223→            )
   224→        )
   225→    else:
   226→        # Only gate dimensions that are actually targeted by this review run.
   227→        blocking_dims = _blocking_scored_dimensions(
   228→            state,
   229→            dimensions=dimensions,
   230→            normalized_dimensions=normalized_dimensions,
   231→        )
   232→
   233→        # No gate when none of the targeted dimensions have prior scores —
   234→        # this is a first run for these dimensions, not a rerun.
   235→        if blocking_dims:
   236→            objective_total, subjective_total = _objective_and_subjective_backlog(
   237→                state,
   238→                blocking_dims=blocking_dims,
   239→            )
   240→            if objective_total > 0 or subjective_total > 0:
   241→                _print_backlog_blocked_message(
   242→                    blocking_dims=blocking_dims,
   243→                    objective_total=objective_total,
   244→                    subjective_total=subjective_total,
   245→                    dimensions=dimensions,
   246→                )
   247→                sys.exit(1)
   248→
   249→    # Gate passed — clear stale for targeted dims
   250→    cleared = clear_stale_subjective_entries(state, dimensions=dimensions)
   251→    if cleared and state_file:
   252→        save_fn(state, state_file)
   253→        print(
   254→            colorize(
   255→                f"  Cleared stale review markers: {', '.join(sorted(cleared))}",
   256→                "cyan",
   257→            )
   258→        )

   286→
   287→def _validate_run_dir(run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, Path, str]:
   288→    """Validate run directory, load summary, and return (summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path).
   289→
   290→    Exits with error message on any validation failure.
   291→    """
   292→    if not run_dir.is_dir():
   293→        print(colorize(f"  Error: run directory not found: {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   294→        sys.exit(1)
   295→
   296→    summary_path = run_dir / "run_summary.json"
   297→    if not summary_path.exists():
   298→        print(colorize(f"  Error: no run_summary.json in {run_dir}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   299→        sys.exit(1)
   300→    try:
   301→        summary = json.loads(summary_path.read_text())
   302→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   303→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading run summary: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   304→        sys.exit(1)
   305→
   306→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   307→    blind_packet_path = Path(str(summary.get("blind_packet", "")))
   308→    immutable_packet_path = str(summary.get("immutable_packet", ""))
   309→
   310→    if not successful:
   311→        print(colorize("  Error: no successful batches in run summary.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   312→        sys.exit(1)
   313→    if not blind_packet_path.exists():
   314→        print(colorize(f"  Error: blind packet not found: {blind_packet_path}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   315→        sys.exit(1)
   316→
   317→    try:
   318→        packet = json.loads(Path(immutable_packet_path).read_text())
   319→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
   320→        print(colorize(f"  Error reading immutable packet: {exc}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   321→        sys.exit(1)
   322→
   323→    summary["_packet"] = packet
   324→    return summary, blind_packet_path, immutable_packet_path
   325→
   326→
   327→def do_import_run(
   328→    run_dir_path: str,
   329→    state: dict,
   330→    lang,
   331→    state_file: str,
   332→    *,
   333→    config: dict | None = None,
   334→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   335→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   336→    scan_path: str = ".",
   337→) -> None:
   338→    """Re-import results from a completed run directory.
   339→
   340→    Replays the merge+provenance+import step that normally runs at the end of
   341→    ``--run-batches``.  Useful when the original pipeline was interrupted (e.g.
   342→    broken pipe from background execution) but all batch results completed.
   343→    """
   344→    run_dir = Path(run_dir_path)
   345→    summary, blind_packet_path, _immutable_path = _validate_run_dir(run_dir)
   346→
   347→    runner = str(summary.get("runner", "codex"))
   348→    stamp = str(summary.get("run_stamp", ""))
   349→    successful = summary.get("successful_batches", [])
   350→    packet = summary.pop("_packet", {})
   351→    allowed_dims = {str(d) for d in packet.get("dimensions", []) if isinstance(d, str)}
   352→
   353→    # -- locate and parse raw batch results --
   354→    results_dir = run_dir / "results"
   355→    selected_indexes = [idx - 1 for idx in successful]  # convert 1-based to 0-based
   356→    output_files = {
   357→        idx: results_dir / f"batch-{idx + 1}.raw.txt"
   358→        for idx in selected_indexes
   359→    }
   360→
   361→    missing = [idx + 1 for idx in selected_indexes if not output_files[idx].exists()]
   362→    if missing:
   363→        print(colorize(f"  Error: missing result files for batches: {missing}", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   364→        sys.exit(1)
   365→
   366→    batch_results, failures = runner_helpers_mod.collect_batch_results(
   367→        selected_indexes=selected_indexes,
   368→        failures=[],
   369→        output_files=output_files,
   370→        allowed_dims=allowed_dims,
   371→        extract_payload_fn=lambda raw: batch_core_mod.extract_json_payload(raw, log_fn=log),
   372→        normalize_result_fn=lambda payload, dims: batch_core_mod.normalize_batch_result(
   373→            payload,
   374→            dims,
   375→            max_batch_findings=max_batch_findings_for_dimension_count(len(dims)),
   376→            abstraction_sub_axes=ABSTRACTION_SUB_AXES,
   377→        ),
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    if not batch_results:
   381→        print(colorize("  Error: no valid batch results could be parsed.", "red"), file=sys.stderr)
   382→        sys.exit(1)
   383→
   384→    print(colorize(f"  Parsed {len(batch_results)} batch results from {run_dir}", "bold"))
   385→    if failures:
   386→        print(colorize(f"  Warning: {len(failures)} batches failed to parse: {[f + 1 for f in failures]}", "yellow"))
   387→
   388→    # -- merge --
   389→    merged = _merge_batch_results(batch_results)
   390→
   391→    # -- build provenance --
   392→    successful_indexes = [idx for idx in selected_indexes if idx not in set(failures)]
   393→    merged["provenance"] = runner_helpers_mod.build_batch_import_provenance(
   394→        runner=runner,
   395→        blind_packet_path=blind_packet_path,
   396→        run_stamp=stamp,
   397→        batch_indexes=successful_indexes,
   398→    )
   399→
   400→    # -- write merged output --
   401→    merged_path = run_dir / "holistic_findings_merged.json"
   402→    safe_write_text(merged_path, json.dumps(merged, indent=2) + "\n")
   403→    print(colorize(f"  Merged output: {merged_path}", "bold"))
   404→
   405→    # -- import with trusted source --
   406→    _do_import(
   407→        str(merged_path),
   408→        state,
   409→        lang,
   410→        state_file,
   411→        config=config,
   412→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   413→        trusted_assessment_source=True,
   414→        trusted_assessment_label=f"trusted import-run replay from {run_dir.name}",
   415→    )
   416→
   417→    # -- optional follow-up scan --
   418→    if scan_after_import:
   419→        lang_name = getattr(lang, "name", None) or str(getattr(lang, "lang", ""))
   420→        if lang_name:
   421→            runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   422→                lang_name=lang_name,
   423→                scan_path=scan_path,
   424→                deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   425→                    project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   426→                    timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   427→                    python_executable=sys.executable,
   428→                    subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   429→                    timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   430→                    colorize_fn=colorize,
   431→                ),
   432→            )
   433→

   374→
   375→def _canonical_external_payload(
   376→    raw_payload: dict[str, Any],
   377→    *,
   378→    session: dict[str, Any],
   379→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   380→    """Return import payload with canonical provenance and required session token."""
   381→    session_meta = raw_payload.get("session")
   382→    if not isinstance(session_meta, dict):
   383→        print(
   384→            colorize(

   386→                "red",

   388→            file=sys.stderr,
   389→        )
   390→        print(
   391→            colorize(
   392→                "  Expected: {\"session\":{\"id\":\"...\",\"token\":\"...\"},\"assessments\":{...},\"findings\":[...]}",
   393→                "dim",
   394→            ),
   395→            file=sys.stderr,
   396→        )
   397→        sys.exit(1)
   398→
   399→    payload_id = str(session_meta.get("id", "")).strip()
   400→    payload_token = str(session_meta.get("token", "")).strip()
   401→    expected_id = str(session.get("session_id", "")).strip()
   402→    expected_token = str(session.get("token", "")).strip()
   403→    if payload_id != expected_id or payload_token != expected_token:
   404→        print(
   405→            colorize(
   406→                "  Error: session id/token mismatch in external reviewer payload.",
   407→                "red",
   408→            ),
   409→            file=sys.stderr,
   410→        )
   411→        print(

   413→            file=sys.stderr,
   414→        )
   415→        sys.exit(1)
   416→
   417→    payload = dict(raw_payload)
   418→    payload.pop("session", None)
   419→    payload.pop("provenance", None)
   420→    payload["provenance"] = {

   422→        "blind": True,
   423→        "runner": str(session.get("runner", "claude")),
   424→        "run_stamp": str(session.get("session_id", "")),
   425→        "created_at": _iso_seconds(_utc_now()),
   426→        "packet_path": str(session.get("blind_packet_path", "")),
   427→        "packet_sha256": str(session.get("packet_sha256", "")),
   428→        "external_session_id": expected_id,
   429→    }
   430→    return payload

   433→def _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   434→    status = str(session.get("status", "open")).strip().lower()
   435→    if status == "open":
   436→        return
   437→    print(
   438→        colorize(
   439→            f"  Error: session is not open (status={status or 'unknown'}). Start a new session with --external-start.",
   440→            "red",
   441→        ),
   442→        file=sys.stderr,
   443→    )
   444→    sys.exit(1)
   445→
   446→
   447→def _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   448→    expires_at = _parse_iso(session.get("expires_at"))
   449→    if expires_at is None:
   450→        print(
   451→            colorize(
   452→                "  Error: session metadata is missing/invalid expires_at.",
   453→                "red",
   454→            ),
   455→            file=sys.stderr,
   456→        )
   457→        sys.exit(1)
   458→    now = _utc_now()
   459→    if now <= expires_at:
   460→        return
   461→    print(
   462→        colorize(
   463→            f"  Error: session expired at {session.get('expires_at')}. Start a new session with --external-start.",
   464→            "red",
   465→        ),
   466→        file=sys.stderr,
   467→    )
   468→    sys.exit(1)
   469→
   470→
   471→def do_external_submit(
   472→    *,
   473→    import_file: str,
   474→    session_id: str,
   475→    state: dict,
   476→    lang,
   477→    state_file,
   478→    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   479→    allow_partial: bool = False,
   480→    scan_after_import: bool = False,
   481→    scan_path: str = ".",
   482→    dry_run: bool = False,
   483→) -> None:
   484→    """Submit external reviewer output via session, adding canonical provenance."""
   485→    config = config or {}
   486→    session_path, session = _session_payload_or_exit(session_id)
   487→    _ensure_session_open_or_exit(session)
   488→    _ensure_session_not_expired_or_exit(session)
   489→
   490→    if str(session.get("runner", "")).strip().lower() not in _EXTERNAL_SUPPORTED_RUNNERS:
   491→        print(
   492→            colorize(
   493→                "  Error: only Claude external sessions currently support durable score submit.",
   494→                "red",
   495→            ),
   496→            file=sys.stderr,
   497→        )
   498→        sys.exit(1)
   499→
   500→    findings_path = Path(import_file)
   501→    raw_payload = _load_json_object(findings_path, label="external findings")
   502→    canonical_payload = _canonical_external_payload(raw_payload, session=session)
   503→
   504→    stamp = runner_helpers_mod.run_stamp()
   505→    session_dir = session_path.parent
   506→    canonical_path = session_dir / f"canonical_import_{stamp}.json"
   507→    safe_write_text(canonical_path, json.dumps(canonical_payload, indent=2) + "\n")
   508→
   509→    if dry_run:
   510→        do_validate_import(
   511→            str(canonical_path),
   512→            lang,
   513→            allow_partial=allow_partial,
   514→            attested_external=True,
   515→            manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   516→        )
   517→        return
   518→
   519→    do_import(
   520→        str(canonical_path),
   521→        state,
   522→        lang,
   523→        state_file,
   524→        config=config,
   525→        allow_partial=allow_partial,
   526→        attested_external=True,
   527→        manual_attest=str(session.get("attest", EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT)),
   528→    )
   529→
   530→    submitted_at = _iso_seconds(_utc_now())
   531→    session["status"] = "submitted"
   532→    session["submitted_at"] = submitted_at
   533→    session["submitted_input_file"] = str(findings_path)
   534→    session["submitted_canonical_file"] = str(canonical_path)
   535→    safe_write_text(session_path, json.dumps(session, indent=2) + "\n")
   536→
   537→    if scan_after_import:
   538→        code = runner_helpers_mod.run_followup_scan(
   539→            lang_name=lang.name,
   540→            scan_path=scan_path,
   541→            deps=runner_helpers_mod.FollowupScanDeps(
   542→                project_root=_runtime_project_root(),
   543→                timeout_seconds=FOLLOWUP_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   544→                python_executable=sys.executable,
   545→                subprocess_run=subprocess.run,
   546→                timeout_error=subprocess.TimeoutExpired,
   547→                colorize_fn=colorize,
   548→            ),
   549→        )
   550→        if code != 0:
   551→            raise SystemExit(code)
   552→
   553→
   554→__all__ = ["do_external_start", "do_external_submit", "EXTERNAL_ATTEST_TEXT"]
   555→

   102→def _collect_reviewed_files_from_batches(
   103→    *,
   104→    batches: list[dict[str, object]],
   105→    selected_indexes: list[int],
   106→) -> list[str]:
   107→    """Collect normalized file paths reviewed in the selected batch set."""
   108→    reviewed: list[str] = []
   109→    seen: set[str] = set()
   110→    for idx in selected_indexes:
   111→        if idx < 0 or idx >= len(batches):
   112→            continue
   113→        batch = batches[idx]
   114→        files = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   115→        if not isinstance(files, list):
   116→            continue
   117→        for raw in files:
   118→            if not isinstance(raw, str):
   119→                continue
   120→            path = raw.strip().strip(",'\"")
   121→            if not path or path in {".", ".."}:
   122→                continue
   123→            if path.endswith("/"):
   124→                continue
   125→            if path in seen:
   126→                continue
   127→            seen.add(path)
   128→            reviewed.append(path)
   129→    return reviewed
   130→
   131→
   132→def _normalize_dimension_list(raw: object) -> list[str]:
   133→    """Normalize dimension collections to a stable, de-duplicated list."""
   134→    if not isinstance(raw, list):
   135→        return []
   136→    out: list[str] = []
   137→    seen: set[str] = set()
   138→    for item in raw:
   139→        if not isinstance(item, str):
   140→            continue
   141→        dim = item.strip()
   142→        if not dim or dim in seen:
   143→            continue
   144→        seen.add(dim)
   145→        out.append(dim)
   146→    return out

   254→def _normalize_heartbeat_payload(
   255→    details: dict[str, object],
   256→) -> tuple[list[int], list[int], dict[int, object]]:
   257→    active = details.get("active_batches")
   258→    queued = details.get("queued_batches", [])
   259→    elapsed = details.get("elapsed_seconds", {})
   260→    active_list = active if isinstance(active, list) else []
   261→    queued_list = queued if isinstance(queued, list) else []
   262→    elapsed_map = elapsed if isinstance(elapsed, dict) else {}
   263→    return active_list, queued_list, elapsed_map
   264→
   265→
   266→def _elapsed_seconds_for(elapsed: dict[int, object], index: int) -> int:
   267→    raw_secs = elapsed.get(index, 0)
   268→    return int(raw_secs) if isinstance(raw_secs, int | float) else 0
   269→
   270→
   271→def _heartbeat_segments(active: list[int], elapsed: dict[int, object]) -> list[str]:
   272→    segments: list[str] = []
   273→    for idx in active[:6]:
   274→        segments.append(f"#{idx + 1}:{_elapsed_seconds_for(elapsed, idx)}s")
   275→    if len(active) > 6:
   276→        segments.append(f"+{len(active) - 6} more")
   277→    return segments
   278→
   279→
   280→def _heartbeat_elapsed_log(active: list[int], elapsed: dict[int, object]) -> str:
   281→    return ", ".join(f"{idx + 1}:{elapsed.get(idx, 0)}" for idx in active)
   282→
   283→
   284→def _slow_active_batches(
   285→    active: list[int],
   286→    *,
   287→    elapsed: dict[int, object],
   288→    threshold: int,
   289→) -> list[int]:
   290→    return [
   291→        idx
   292→        for idx in active
   293→        if _elapsed_seconds_for(elapsed, idx) >= threshold
   294→    ]

   117→def _progress_contract(
   118→    progress_fn,
   119→    *,
   120→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   121→) -> str:
   122→    """Resolve callback contract once: ``event`` or ``legacy``."""
   123→    if not callable(progress_fn):
   124→        return "none"
   125→    fn_id = id(progress_fn)
   126→    cache = contract_cache if contract_cache is not None else {}
   127→    cached = cache.get(fn_id)
   128→    if cached:
   129→        return cached
   130→    try:
   131→        signature = inspect.signature(progress_fn)
   132→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
   133→        contract = "event"
   134→    else:
   135→        required_positional = 0
   136→        for param in signature.parameters.values():
   137→            if param.kind not in (
   138→                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_ONLY,
   139→                inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD,
   140→            ):
   141→                continue
   142→            if param.default is inspect.Signature.empty:
   143→                required_positional += 1
   144→        # Legacy callbacks require at least (batch_index, event).
   145→        contract = "legacy" if required_positional >= 2 else "event"
   146→    cache[fn_id] = contract
   147→    return contract
   148→
   149→
   150→def _emit_progress(
   151→    progress_fn,
   152→    batch_index: int,
   153→    event: str,
   154→    code: int | None = None,
   155→    *,
   156→    details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   157→    contract_cache: dict[int, str] | None = None,
   158→) -> Exception | None:
   159→    """Forward a progress event and return callback exceptions to caller."""
   160→    contract = _progress_contract(progress_fn, contract_cache=contract_cache)
   161→    if contract == "none":
   162→        return None
   163→    payload = dict(details or {})
   164→    progress_event = BatchProgressEvent(
   165→        batch_index=batch_index,
   166→        event=event,
   167→        code=code,
   168→        details=payload,
   169→    )
   170→    try:
   171→        if contract == "legacy":
   172→            progress_fn(batch_index, event, code, **payload)
   173→        else:
   174→            progress_fn(progress_event)
   175→        return None
   176→    except _RUNNER_CALLBACK_EXCEPTIONS as exc:
   177→        return RuntimeError(
   178→            f"progress callback failed for event={event} batch={batch_index}: {exc}"
   179→        )
   180→
   181→
   182→def _record_execution_error(
   183→    *,
   184→    error_log_fn,
   185→    failures: set[int],
   186→    idx: int,
   187→    exc: Exception,
   188→) -> None:
   189→    """Record an execution/progress error through shared failure plumbing."""
   190→    if callable(error_log_fn):
   191→        try:
   192→            error_log_fn(idx, exc)
   193→        except (OSError, TypeError, ValueError) as err:
   194→            log_best_effort_failure(
   195→                logger,
   196→                "record batch execution error via callback",
   197→                err,
   198→            )
   199→    failures.add(idx)

   212→    Each value in *tasks* is a zero-arg callable returning an int exit code.
   213→    All domain knowledge (files, prompts, etc.) is pre-bound by the caller.

   291→                idx=idx,
   292→                exc=done_error,
   293→            )

   181→        stat = output_file.stat()
   182→    except OSError as exc:
   183→        return f"{output_file} (exists; stat failed: {exc})"
   184→    modified_at = datetime.fromtimestamp(stat.st_mtime, tz=UTC).isoformat(
   185→        timespec="seconds"
   186→    )
   187→    return (
   188→        f"{output_file} (exists; bytes={stat.st_size}; "
   189→        f"modified={modified_at})"
   190→    )
   191→
   192→
   193→def _output_file_has_json_payload(output_file: Path) -> bool:
   194→    """Return True when the output file contains a valid JSON object."""
   195→    if not output_file.exists():
   196→        return False
   197→    try:
   198→        payload = json.loads(output_file.read_text())
   199→    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   200→        return False

    21→DEFAULT_BATCH_STALL_KILL_SECONDS = 360
    22→
    23→
    24→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    25→class BatchRunPolicy:
    26→    """Resolved runtime knobs for `review --run-batches` execution."""
    27→
    28→    run_parallel: bool
    29→    max_parallel_batches: int
    30→    heartbeat_seconds: float
    31→    batch_timeout_seconds: int
    32→    batch_max_retries: int
    33→    batch_retry_backoff_seconds: float
    34→    stall_warning_seconds: int
    35→    stall_kill_seconds: int
    36→
    37→    def max_parallel_workers(self, total_batches: int) -> int:
    38→        if total_batches <= 0:
    39→            return 1
    40→        if self.run_parallel:
    41→            return min(total_batches, self.max_parallel_batches)
    42→        return 1
    43→
    44→    def worst_case_minutes(self, total_batches: int) -> int:
    45→        waves = math.ceil(total_batches / self.max_parallel_workers(total_batches))
    46→        return max(1, math.ceil((waves * self.batch_timeout_seconds) / 60))
    47→
    48→
    49→def resolve_batch_run_policy(args) -> BatchRunPolicy:
    50→    """Build one canonical policy object from CLI args."""
    51→    return BatchRunPolicy(
    52→        run_parallel=bool(getattr(args, "parallel", False)),
    53→        max_parallel_batches=_coerce_positive_int(
    54→            getattr(args, "max_parallel_batches", None),

    56→            minimum=1,

### 3. TWO BATCH EXECUTION IMPLEMENTATIONS IDENTIFIED

**LEGACY/WRAPPER LAYER (batch.py):**
- Line 181: `_do_run_batches(args, state, lang, state_file, config)`
- **Purpose:** Entry point from entrypoint.py for `--run-batches`
- **What it does:**
  1. Loads/prepares packet via `_load_or_prepare_packet()` (lines 93-178)
  2. Creates dependency injection lambdas wrapping batches_runtime + runner_helpers functions
  3. Calls `batches.do_run_batches()` with all dependencies injected
- **Why it exists:** Decouples CLI args from core batches.py logic via DI

**NEW/CORE LAYER (batches.py):**
- Line 409: `do_run_batches(args, state, lang, state_file, *, config, run_stamp_fn, load_or_prepare_packet_fn, ...)`
- **Purpose:** Actual orchestration logic
- **What it does:**
  1. Validates runner
  2. Resolves batch run policy
  3. Loads/prepares packet
  4. Selects batch indexes
  5. Prepares run artifacts (prompts, logs, directories)
  6. Executes batches via `execute_batches_fn`
  7. Collects results & handles failures
  8. Merges results
  9. Imports via `do_import_fn`
  10. Optional follow-up scan

**The Split:** batch.py is a thin wrapper (4-5 levels of lambda nesting) that injects 10+ dependency functions into batches.py

---

### 4. PACKET PREPARATION DUPLICATION

**Three implementations of packet preparation:**

**batch.py lines 93-178:** `_load_or_prepare_packet()`
- Handles packet override or fresh preparation
- Calls `_setup_lang()` to setup language runtime
- Calls `narrative_mod.compute_narrative()`
- Calls `review_mod.prepare_holistic_review()`
- Writes packet + blind packet snapshots
- **Returns:** (packet, packet_path, blind_path)

**external.py lines 137-194:** `_prepare_packet_snapshot()`
- Nearly identical to batch.py's implementation
- **Key difference:** packet["config"] NOT set (batch.py does)
- Uses `write_query()` instead of `write_query_best_effort()`
- **Returns:** (packet, packet_path, blind_path)

**prepare.py lines 19-102:** `do_prepare()`
- Standalone mode (no execution)
- Same packet preparation logic
- Writes to query.json only, no execution

**Duplication:** Lines 120-178 (batch.py) vs 145-173 (external.py) are ~95% identical

### 6. BATCHES_RUNTIME.PY VS BATCHES.PY

**batches_runtime.py (430 lines):**
- **NEW/MODERN layer** - extracted state/progress tracking
- Contains:
  - `BatchRunSummaryConfig` - immutable config for summary writing
  - `BatchProgressTracker` - mutable state machine for batch lifecycle
  - `write_run_summary()` - writes run_summary.json
  - `build_batch_tasks()` - builds index→callable map
  - `make_run_log_writer()` - creates log appender
  - `resolve_run_log_path()` - path resolution
  - `_run_batch_task()` - task executor
- **Design:** Data containers + free functions (functional style)
- **Used by:** batches.py calls it

**batches.py (916 lines):**
- **Main orchestration** 
- Do_run_batches() orchestrates the entire flow
- Lines 409-550+: Main loop
- Takes ALL 22+ dependency injection functions as kwargs
- **Design:** Stateless orchestration function

**Relationship:** batches_runtime provides the state/progress infrastructure; batches.py uses it

---

### 7. RUNNER_PARALLEL.PY VS RUNNER_HELPERS.PY

**runner_parallel.py (659 lines):**
- **Pure execution layer** - no subprocess knowledge
- Contains:
  - `BatchTask` - type alias for `Callable[[], int]`
  - `BatchProgressEvent` - typed event dataclass
  - `BatchExecutionOptions` - runtime options (parallel, heartbeat, etc.)
  - `execute_batches()` - **Main entry point** (returns failure list)
  - `_execute_serial()` - serial task runner
  - `_execute_parallel()` - parallel with ThreadPoolExecutor + heartbeat
  - `_emit_progress()` - callback dispatcher (legacy vs typed event contract)
  - `_progress_contract()` - signature introspection for callback compat

**runner_helpers.py (1190 lines):**
- **Orchestration coordinator** - re-exports from runner_parallel + runner_process
- Contains:
  - `CodexBatchRunnerDeps` - deps dataclass
  - `FollowupScanDeps` - follow-up scan deps
  - `BatchResult` - typed result (to_dict for backward compat)
  - `BatchProgressEvent` - duplicate (also in runner_parallel)
  - `run_codex_batch()` - main subprocess runner (calls runner_process)
  - `execute_batches()` - thin wrapper over runner_parallel.execute_batches()
  - `build_blind_packet()` - packet sanitization
  - `collect_batch_results()` - result collection + normalization
  - `print_failures()` - failure reporting
  - `run_followup_scan()` - scan subprocess
  - Many re-exports from runner_packets, runner_process, runner_parallel

**Duplication:**
- `CodexBatchRunnerDeps` defined in BOTH files (lines 25-36 in runner_process, 66-77 in runner_helpers)
- `FollowupScanDeps` defined in BOTH files (lines 40-46 in runner_process, 81-87 in runner_helpers)
- `BatchProgressEvent` defined in BOTH files (runner_parallel lines 45-51, runner_helpers lines 112-118)
- `_RunnerState`, `_AttemptContext`, `_ExecutionResult` defined in BOTH files

**Design Intent:**
- runner_parallel: Pure execution (serial/parallel dispatch)
- runner_process: Subprocess management (codex invocation)
- runner_helpers: Coordinator that ties them together + provides orchestration

---

### 8. RUNNER_PROCESS.PY ROLE

**runner_process.py (723 lines):**
- **Subprocess executor for codex batch runs**
- Entry point: `run_codex_batch()` (signature at line ~400+)
- Contains:
  - `codex_batch_command()` - builds `codex exec ...` CLI
  - `_run_via_subprocess()` - uses subprocess.run()
  - `_run_via_popen()` - uses subprocess.Popen() for live streaming
  - `_write_live_snapshot()` - writes live log during execution
  - `_collect_stream()` - streams output chunks
  - Retry logic & stall detection
  - Output file validation (`_output_file_has_json_payload()`)

**Key responsibility:** Invoke codex subagent, capture output, detect failures/timeouts/stalls, handle retries

### 9. ACTUAL CODE ENTRY POINTS FROM CLI

**entrypoint.py: cmd_review()**
```
1. cmd_review() [line 189] ← Entry from CLI
   ↓
2. _mode_flags() [line 43] → Parse which mode
   ↓
3. _run_review_mode() [line 102] → Dispatch to one of:
   - do_merge()  [line 113]
   - _do_run_batches() [line 117]  ← LOCAL BATCH RUN
   - do_import_run() [line 127]  ← REPLAY RUN RESULTS
   - do_external_start() [line 140]  ← START EXTERNAL SESSION
   - do_external_submit() [line 148]  ← SUBMIT EXTERNAL SESSION
   - do_validate_import() [line 162]  ← VALIDATE IMPORT FILE
   - do_import() [line 173]  ← IMPORT FINDINGS
   - do_prepare() [line 186]  ← PREPARE PACKET ONLY
```

**Each mode flow:**

1. **`--run-batches`** → `_do_run_batches()` (batch.py:181) → `batches.do_run_batches()` (batches.py:409) → execution loop
2. **`--external-start`** → `do_external_start()` (external.py:245) → creates session directory + artifacts
3. **`--external-submit`** → `do_external_submit()` (external.py:471) → validates session + imports
4. **`--import-run`** → `do_import_run()` (batch.py:327) → replays run results from directory
5. **`--import`** → `do_import()` (import_cmd.py) → imports findings.json directly
6. **`--prepare`** → `do_prepare()` (prepare.py:19) → packet preparation only
7. **`--merge`** → `do_merge()` (merge.py) → manual merge CLI

---

### KEY ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHTS

**The Duplication Pattern:**
1. **batch.py** = thin wrapper (DI layer) around batches.py
2. **batches.py** = core orchestration (22+ injected functions)
3. **batches_runtime.py** = extracted state/progress tracking
4. **runner_helpers.py** = coordinator re-exporting from runner_parallel + runner_process
5. **runner_parallel.py** = pure execution (serial/parallel dispatch)
6. **runner_process.py** = subprocess management (codex invocation)

**Three Packet Preparations:**
- batch.py (local run)
- external.py (cloud session)
- prepare.py (packet-only)

**Why the duplication exists:**
- DI layer (batch.py) to decouple CLI args from core logic
- State extraction (batches_runtime.py) for progress tracking
- Coordinator pattern (runner_helpers.py) to integrate execution layers
- Subprocess abstraction (runner_process.py) to handle complexity

**Total review package:** 11,107 lines across 34 files

   331→_DISPLAY_ORDER = list(DISPLAY_ORDER)
   332→
   333→JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
   334→    name for name, meta in DETECTORS.items() if meta.needs_judgment
   335→)
   336→_BASE_DETECTORS: dict[str, DetectorMeta] = dict(DETECTORS)
   337→_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER: list[str] = list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   338→_BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(JUDGMENT_DETECTORS)
   339→
   340→_on_register_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
   341→
   342→
   343→def on_detector_registered(callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
   344→    """Register a callback invoked after register_detector(). No-arg."""
   345→    _on_register_callbacks.append(callback)
   346→
   347→
   348→def register_detector(meta: DetectorMeta) -> None:
   349→    """Register a detector at runtime (used by generic plugins)."""
   350→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   351→    DETECTORS[meta.name] = meta
   352→    if meta.name not in _DISPLAY_ORDER:
   353→        _DISPLAY_ORDER.append(meta.name)
   354→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = frozenset(
   355→        name for name, m in DETECTORS.items() if m.needs_judgment
   356→    )
   357→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   358→        cb()
   359→
   360→
   361→def reset_registered_detectors() -> None:
   362→    """Reset runtime-added detector registrations to built-in defaults."""
   363→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   364→    DETECTORS.clear()
   365→    DETECTORS.update(_BASE_DETECTORS)
   366→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.clear()
   367→    _DISPLAY_ORDER.extend(_BASE_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   368→    JUDGMENT_DETECTORS = _BASE_JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   369→    for cb in _on_register_callbacks:
   370→        cb()
   371→
   372→
   373→def detector_names() -> list[str]:
   374→    """All registered detector names, sorted."""
   375→    return sorted(DETECTORS.keys())
   376→
   377→
   378→def display_order() -> list[str]:
   379→    """Canonical display order for terminal output."""
   380→    return list(_DISPLAY_ORDER)
   381→
   382→
   383→_ACTION_PRIORITY = {"auto_fix": 0, "reorganize": 1, "refactor": 2, "manual_fix": 3}
   384→_ACTION_LABELS = {
   385→    "auto_fix": "fix",
   386→    "reorganize": "move",
   387→    "refactor": "refactor",
   388→    "manual_fix": "manual",
   389→}
   390→
   391→
   392→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   393→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   394→    best = "manual"
   395→    best_pri = 99
   396→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   397→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   398→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   399→            if pri < best_pri:
   400→                best_pri = pri
   401→                best = d.action_type
   402→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")
   403→
   404→
   405→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   406→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   407→    result = {}
   408→    for name, d in DETECTORS.items():
   409→        entry: dict = {
   410→            "fixers": list(d.fixers),
   411→            "action_type": d.action_type,
   412→        }
   413→        if d.tool:
   414→            entry["tool"] = d.tool
   415→        if d.guidance:
   416→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   417→        result[name] = entry
   418→    return result

   102→def _extract_prompt_meta(entry: object) -> dict[str, object]:
   103→    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
   104→        return {}
   105→    meta = entry.get("meta")
   106→    if not isinstance(meta, dict):
   107→        return {}
   108→    out: dict[str, object] = {}
   109→
   110→    if isinstance(meta.get("display_name"), str) and meta["display_name"].strip():
   111→        out["display_name"] = meta["display_name"].strip()
   112→
   113→    weight = meta.get("weight")
   114→    if is_numeric(weight):
   115→        out["weight"] = max(0.0, float(weight))
   116→
   117→    enabled = meta.get("enabled_by_default")
   118→    if isinstance(enabled, bool):
   119→        out["enabled_by_default"] = enabled
   120→
   121→    reset_on_scan = meta.get("reset_on_scan")
   122→    if isinstance(reset_on_scan, bool):
   123→        out["reset_on_scan"] = reset_on_scan
   124→
   125→    return out
   126→
   127→
   128→def _merge_prompt_display_and_weights(
   129→    payload: dict[str, object],
   130→    *,
   131→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   132→    override_existing: bool,
   133→) -> None:
   134→    if "display_name" in prompt_meta and (
   135→        override_existing or "display_name" not in payload
   136→    ):
   137→        payload["display_name"] = prompt_meta["display_name"]
   138→    if "weight" in prompt_meta and (override_existing or "weight" not in payload):
   139→        payload["weight"] = prompt_meta["weight"]
   140→    if "reset_on_scan" in prompt_meta and (
   141→        override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload
   142→    ):
   143→        payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]
   144→
   145→
   146→def _merge_enabled_by_default_flag(
   147→    payload: dict[str, object],
   148→    *,
   149→    prompt_meta: dict[str, object],
   150→    override_existing: bool,
   151→    default_enabled: bool,
   152→) -> None:
   153→    if default_enabled:
   154→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
   155→    if "enabled_by_default" not in prompt_meta:
   156→        return
   157→    prompt_enabled = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
   158→    if override_existing:
   159→        payload["enabled_by_default"] = prompt_enabled
   160→        return
   161→    payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
   162→        payload.get("enabled_by_default", False) or prompt_enabled

   174→def _merge_dimension_meta(

   259→def configure_subjective_dimension_providers(
   260→    *,
   261→    available_languages_provider: Callable[[], list[str]] | None = None,
   262→    load_dimensions_payload_provider: Callable[
   263→        [], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   264→    ]

   266→    load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider: Callable[
   267→        [str], tuple[list[str], dict[str, dict[str, object]], str]
   268→    ]
   269→    | None = None,
   270→) -> None:
   271→    """Configure metadata providers for subjective-dimension lookups."""
   272→    state = _PROVIDER_STATE
   273→
   274→    changed = False
   275→    if (
   276→        available_languages_provider is not None
   277→        and available_languages_provider is not state.available_languages_provider
   278→    ):
   279→        state.available_languages_provider = available_languages_provider
   280→        changed = True
   281→    if (
   282→        load_dimensions_payload_provider is not None
   283→        and load_dimensions_payload_provider
   284→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_provider
   285→    ):
   286→        state.load_dimensions_payload_provider = load_dimensions_payload_provider
   287→        changed = True
   288→    if (
   289→        load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider is not None
   290→        and load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   291→        is not state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   292→    ):
   293→        state.load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider = (
   294→            load_dimensions_payload_for_lang_provider
   295→        )

   311→def _normalize_dimension_list(values: list[str]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   312→    normalized: list[str] = []
   313→    for raw in values:
   314→        if not isinstance(raw, str):
   315→            continue
   316→        dim = _normalize_dimension_name(raw)
   317→        if not dim or dim in normalized:
   318→            continue
   319→        normalized.append(dim)
   320→    return tuple(normalized)

   326→    try:
   327→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   328→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   329→        logger.debug("Failed to load default subjective dimensions: %s", exc)
   330→        return tuple(_LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.keys())
   331→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)

   335→def default_dimension_keys_for_lang(lang_name: str | None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   336→    """Return default subjective dimension keys for a specific language."""
   337→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   338→    if normalized is None:
   339→        return default_dimension_keys()
   340→    try:
   341→        dims, _, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(normalized)
   342→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   343→        logger.debug(
   344→            "Failed to load subjective dimensions for lang %s: %s",
   345→            normalized,
   346→            exc,
   347→        )
   348→        return default_dimension_keys()
   349→    return _normalize_dimension_list(dims)

   352→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   353→    *,
   354→    lang_name: str | None,
   355→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   356→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   357→
   358→    try:
   359→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload()
   360→    except (ImportError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   361→        logger.debug("Failed to load shared subjective dimension payload: %s", exc)
   362→        shared_defaults, shared_prompts = [], {}
   363→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   364→
   365→    langs = (
   366→        [lang_name]
   367→        if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip()
   368→        else _available_languages()
   369→    )
   370→    for name in langs:
   371→        try:
   372→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = _load_dimensions_payload_for_lang(name)
   373→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   374→                out,
   375→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   376→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   377→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   378→            )
   379→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   380→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   381→            continue
   382→
   383→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   384→        payload.setdefault(
   385→            "display_name",
   386→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   387→        )
   388→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   389→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   390→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   391→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   392→        else:
   393→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   394→
   395→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   396→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   397→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   398→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   399→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   400→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   401→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   402→
   403→    return out
   404→

   406→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   407→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   408→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   409→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   410→
   411→
   412→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   413→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   414→    lang_name: str | None,
   415→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   416→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   417→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   418→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   419→

   421→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   422→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   423→    if normalized is None:
   424→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   425→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   426→
   427→
   428→def get_dimension_metadata(
   429→    dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None
   430→) -> dict[str, object]:
   431→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   432→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   433→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   434→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   435→
   436→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   437→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   438→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   439→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   440→    return payload
   441→
   442→
   443→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   444→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   445→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   446→
   447→
   448→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   449→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   450→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   451→    if is_numeric(raw):
   452→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   453→    return 1.0
   454→
   455→
   456→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   457→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   458→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   459→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   460→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   461→            continue
   462→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   463→    return out
   464→
   465→
   466→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   467→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   468→    out = []
   469→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   470→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   471→            continue
   472→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   473→            continue
   474→        out.append(dim)
   475→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))

1→"""Load and validate review dimension payloads from JSON data files."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import copy
     6→import json
     7→from functools import lru_cache
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.review.feedback_contract import ensure_prompt_contract
    11→from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.validation import (
    12→    parse_dimensions_payload,
    13→)
    14→
    15→_LANG_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "languages"
    16→_LANG_DATA_SUBDIR = "review_data"
    17→_DATA_DIR = _LANG_DIR / "_framework" / _LANG_DATA_SUBDIR
    18→
    19→# Canonical filename for the unified dimensions payload.
    20→_DIMENSIONS_FILE = "dimensions.json"
    21→
    22→
    23→def _load_json_payload_from_path(path: Path) -> dict:
    24→    """Load a JSON payload from *path* and return a dict."""
    25→    try:
    26→        raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    27→    except OSError as exc:
    28→        raise RuntimeError(f"Unable to read dimensions payload: {path}") from exc
    29→
    30→    try:
    31→        payload = json.loads(raw)
    32→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
    33→        raise ValueError(f"Invalid JSON in dimensions payload: {path}") from exc
    34→
    35→    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    36→        raise ValueError(f"Dimensions payload must be a JSON object: {path}")
    37→    return payload
    38→
    39→
    40→def _lang_payload_path(lang_name: str, filename: str) -> Path:
    41→    """Resolve the per-language review payload path."""
    42→    return _LANG_DIR / lang_name / _LANG_DATA_SUBDIR / filename
    43→
    44→
    45→def _override_filename(filename: str) -> str:
    46→    """Convert ``foo.json`` to ``foo.override.json``."""
    47→    if not filename.endswith(".json"):
    48→        return f"{filename}.override.json"
    49→    return f"{filename[:-5]}.override.json"
    50→
    51→
    52→def _load_json_payload(filename: str) -> dict:
    53→    """Load a JSON payload from the shared language review-data directory."""
    54→    return _load_json_payload_from_path(_DATA_DIR / filename)
    55→
    56→
    57→def _validate_optional_string_list(value: object, *, context: str) -> list[str]:
    58→    """Validate an optional list of strings (empty allowed)."""
    59→    if value is None:
    60→        return []
    61→    if not isinstance(value, list):
    62→        raise ValueError(f"{context} must be a list of strings")
    63→    out: list[str] = []
    64→    for idx, item in enumerate(value):
    65→        if not isinstance(item, str) or not item.strip():
    66→            raise ValueError(f"{context}[{idx}] must be a non-empty string")
    67→        out.append(item)
    68→    return out
    69→
    70→
    71→def _apply_dimensions_override(
    72→    base_payload: dict,
    73→    override_payload: dict,
    74→    *,
    75→    dims_key: str,
    76→    context: str,
    77→) -> dict:
    78→    """Apply a language override payload to a base dimensions payload."""
    79→    if not isinstance(override_payload, dict):
    80→        raise ValueError(f"{context} must be a JSON object")
    81→
    82→    allowed = {
    83→        dims_key,
    84→        f"{dims_key}_append",
    85→        f"{dims_key}_remove",
    86→        "dimension_prompts",
    87→        "dimension_prompts_remove",
    88→        "system_prompt",
    89→        "system_prompt_append",
    90→    }
    91→    actual = set(override_payload)
    92→    extra = sorted(actual - allowed)
    93→    if extra:
    94→        raise ValueError(f"{context} has unsupported keys: {extra}")
    95→
    96→    out = copy.deepcopy(base_payload)
    97→
    98→    if dims_key in override_payload:
    99→        out[dims_key] = override_payload[dims_key]
   100→
   101→    dims = list(out.get(dims_key, []))
   102→    for dim in _validate_optional_string_list(
   103→        override_payload.get(f"{dims_key}_append"),
   104→        context=f"{context}.{dims_key}_append",
   105→    ):
   106→        if dim not in dims:
   107→            dims.append(dim)
   108→
   109→    remove_dims = set(
   110→        _validate_optional_string_list(
   111→            override_payload.get(f"{dims_key}_remove"),
   112→            context=f"{context}.{dims_key}_remove",
   113→        )
   114→    )
   115→    if remove_dims:
   116→        dims = [dim for dim in dims if dim not in remove_dims]
   117→    out[dims_key] = dims
   118→
   119→    if "dimension_prompts" in override_payload:
   120→        prompt_overrides = override_payload["dimension_prompts"]
   121→        if not isinstance(prompt_overrides, dict):
   122→            raise ValueError(f"{context}.dimension_prompts must be an object")
   123→        prompts = dict(out.get("dimension_prompts", {}))
   124→        for dim_name, prompt in prompt_overrides.items():
   125→            prompts[dim_name] = prompt
   126→        out["dimension_prompts"] = prompts
   127→
   128→    remove_prompts = _validate_optional_string_list(
   129→        override_payload.get("dimension_prompts_remove"),
   130→        context=f"{context}.dimension_prompts_remove",
   131→    )
   132→    if remove_prompts:
   133→        prompts = dict(out.get("dimension_prompts", {}))
   134→        for dim_name in remove_prompts:
   135→            prompts.pop(dim_name, None)
   136→        out["dimension_prompts"] = prompts
   137→
   138→    if "system_prompt" in override_payload:
   139→        out["system_prompt"] = override_payload["system_prompt"]
   140→    if "system_prompt_append" in override_payload:
   141→        suffix = override_payload["system_prompt_append"]
   142→        if not isinstance(suffix, str):
   143→            raise ValueError(f"{context}.system_prompt_append must be a string")
   144→        current = out.get("system_prompt", "")
   145→        sep = "\n\n" if current and suffix else ""
   146→        out["system_prompt"] = f"{current}{sep}{suffix}"
   147→
   148→    return out
   149→
   150→

     2→
     3→This module is the single source of truth for import-boundary policy:
     4→- public runtime modules (stable entry surfaces),
     5→- deprecated compatibility modules (removal candidates),
     6→- private modules (internal implementation details).
     7→"""
     8→

    11→from collections.abc import Iterable

    13→

    20→    "desloppify.languages",

    41→        "search",

    48→PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES: tuple[str, ...] = ("desloppify.core",)

    52→    """Return True when module is a soft-deprecated compatibility surface."""

    55→

    57→    """Return True when module path belongs to a private internal namespace."""
    58→    normalized = module.strip()
    59→    if not normalized:
    60→        return False
    61→    for prefix in PRIVATE_MODULE_PREFIXES:
    62→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    63→            return True
    64→    return False
    65→
    66→
    67→def importer_can_access_private(importer_module: str) -> bool:
    68→    """Return True when importer module is allowed to reference private APIs."""
    69→    normalized = importer_module.strip()
    70→    if not normalized:
    71→        return False
    72→    for prefix in PRIVATE_ALLOWED_IMPORTER_PREFIXES:
    73→        if normalized == prefix or normalized.startswith(f"{prefix}."):
    74→            return True
    75→    return False
    76→
    77→
    78→def iter_soft_deprecated_module_paths() -> Iterable[str]:
    79→    """Yield python-module relative paths for deprecated compatibility modules."""
    80→    for module in sorted(SOFT_DEPRECATED_MODULES):
    81→        parts = module.split(".")
    82→        yield "/".join(parts) + ".py"
